intro.title: animation fill-mode and direction
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple animation of a square that moves across the screen and changes color. You will learn the core CSS concepts of animation-fill-mode and animation-direction to control how an element appears before and after an animation, and whether the animation plays forward, backward, or alternates. The main technologies involved are CSS animations using @keyframes and the animation shorthand properties. By the end, you'll be able to create smooth, controlled animations that enhance user interfaces.
intro.usecase: Animation fill-mode and direction are essential for creating polished loading sequences, progress indicators, and interactive feedback in modern web applications. For example, when a dashboard loads data, you might use animation-fill-mode: forwards to keep progress bars at 100% after completion, preventing them from snapping back. In interactive menus or filters, animation-direction: alternate can create smooth back-and-forth hover effects that enhance user experience. These properties give developers precise control over animation states, ensuring UI elements maintain their intended appearance throughout user interactions.

objectives: Apply the animation-fill-mode property to control element states before and after animation execution
Configure animation-direction values to manipulate playback sequences (normal, reverse, alternate, alternate-reverse)
Construct CSS animations that maintain final frame states using fill-mode settings
Integrate fill-mode and direction properties to create complex animation behaviors
Manipulate animation timing by combining direction with iteration counts
Update existing animations to use appropriate fill-mode values for different UI scenarios
Implement directional animation patterns that respond to user interactions

steps.title: Create HTML structure with animation elements
steps.instruction: Create a basic HTML structure with three div elements that will serve as our animation containers.
steps.hint: Start with a simple HTML structure containing three div elements inside a body tag.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a basic HTML document with three empty div elements ready for styling and animation.
successCriteria: The HTML contains three div elements inside a body tag.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly three div elements inside the body tag.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure doesn't match what we need. Please create an HTML document with three div elements inside a body tag.

steps.title: Define base animation keyframes
steps.instruction: Create a @keyframes rule named 'slide' that moves elements from left to right.
steps.hint: Use @keyframes slide { from { left: 0; } to { left: 100%; } } to define the animation.
steps.expectedOutcome: A @keyframes rule named 'slide' is created, defining movement from left to right.
successCriteria: The code contains a @keyframes rule with the name 'slide' and defines movement from left to right.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your @keyframes rule is named 'slide' and moves elements from left to right.
steps.feedbackWrong: The @keyframes rule is missing or incorrect. Please create a @keyframes rule named 'slide' that moves from left to right.

steps.title: Apply basic animation properties
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule that applies the slide animation to all three div elements with a duration of 2 seconds, an ease-in-out timing function, and an infinite iteration count.
steps.hint: Use the element selector 'div' followed by curly braces. Inside, set the animation property to 'slide' with the specified values.
steps.seedCode: /* Add your @keyframes rule here */ /* Apply animation properties to all div elements */
steps.expectedOutcome: All three boxes will have the slide animation applied with the specified duration, timing, and infinite repetition.
successCriteria: The CSS rule targets all div elements and includes animation: slide 2s ease-in-out infinite;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your rule targets div elements and includes all three properties: animation name, duration, timing function, and iteration count.
steps.feedbackWrong: The animation properties aren't correctly applied. Check that you're using the correct selector and animation syntax.

steps.title: Introduce animation-fill-mode property
steps.instruction: Add the animation-fill-mode property to all div elements and set it to 'forwards' to keep the final animation state.
steps.hint: Use the CSS property animation-fill-mode with the value 'forwards' in the existing rule that targets all div elements.
steps.seedCode: /* Add your @keyframes rule here */ /* Apply animation properties to all div elements */ div { animation-fill-mode: forwards; }
steps.expectedOutcome: The div elements will retain the final style from the animation after it completes.
successCriteria: The CSS rule for div includes the animation-fill-mode property set to 'forwards'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added animation-fill-mode, but check if the value is 'forwards' and it's applied to all div elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding animation-fill-mode: forwards to the div rule. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Apply different fill-mode values
steps.instruction: Set different animation-fill-mode values on each div element: use 'none' for the first div, 'forwards' for the second div (already set), and 'both' for the third div.
steps.hint: Target each div individually using CSS selectors (like div:nth-child(1)) and set the animation-fill-mode property to the specified values.
steps.seedCode: /* Add your @keyframes rule here */ /* Apply animation properties to all div elements */ div { animation-fill-mode: forwards; } /* Set different fill-mode values for each div */
steps.expectedOutcome: Each div element will have a different animation-fill-mode value applied, allowing you to compare their effects.
successCriteria: The first div has animation-fill-mode: none, the second has animation-fill-mode: forwards, and the third has animation-fill-mode: both.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've applied some fill-mode values, but not all three are correctly set. Make sure each div has a unique value: none, forwards, and both.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fill-mode values aren't correctly applied. Check that you're targeting each div individually and setting the animation-fill-mode property with the exact values: none, forwards, both.

steps.title: Introduce animation-direction property
steps.instruction: Add the animation-direction property to the div selector and set its value to 'normal'.
steps.hint: The animation-direction property controls the direction of animation playback. Add it to the existing div rule.
steps.seedCode: /* Add your @keyframes rule here */ /* Apply animation properties to all div elements */ div { animation-fill-mode: forwards; animation-direction: normal; } /* Set different fill-mode values for each div */
steps.expectedOutcome: The animation-direction property is added to control the playback direction of the animation.
successCriteria: The div selector includes the animation-direction property set to 'normal'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the animation-direction property to the div selector with the value 'normal'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The animation-direction property should be added to the div selector. Check the syntax and placement.

steps.title: Apply different direction values
steps.instruction: Set the animation-direction property to 'reverse' for the second div and 'alternate' for the third div in your CSS.
steps.hint: Add two CSS rules: one targeting the second div with animation-direction: reverse, and another targeting the third div with animation-direction: alternate.
steps.seedCode: /* Add your @keyframes rule here */ /* Apply animation properties to all div elements */ div { animation-fill-mode: forwards; animation-direction: normal; } /* Set different fill-mode values for each div */ /* Set different direction values for each div */
steps.expectedOutcome: The second div will animate in reverse, and the third div will alternate between forward and reverse animation cycles.
successCriteria: The second div has animation-direction: reverse and the third div has animation-direction: alternate.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've correctly targeted the second and third divs with the proper direction values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The direction values aren't set correctly. Make sure you're targeting the second div with 'reverse' and the third div with 'alternate'.

steps.title: Combine fill-mode and direction
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS rule for a fourth div element that combines both animation-fill-mode and animation-direction properties with different values.
steps.hint: Add a new CSS selector targeting a fourth div, then set both animation-fill-mode and animation-direction properties with values different from the previous divs.
steps.seedCode: /* Add your @keyframes rule here */ /* Apply animation properties to all div elements */ div { animation-fill-mode: forwards; animation-direction: normal; } /* Set different fill-mode values for each div */ /* Set different direction values for each div */ /* Create a new rule for a fourth div combining both properties */
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule is created that targets a fourth div element and sets both animation-fill-mode and animation-direction properties with specific values.
successCriteria: The code includes a CSS rule for a fourth div element that has both animation-fill-mode and animation-direction properties defined with values different from the previous divs.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your CSS rule targets a fourth div element and includes both animation-fill-mode and animation-direction properties with specific values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The code doesn't yet include a CSS rule for a fourth div element with both animation-fill-mode and animation-direction properties. Try creating a new CSS selector and adding both properties with different values.

steps.title: Add animation-delay to demonstrate backwards fill-mode
steps.instruction: Add an animation-delay property to the fourth div to demonstrate how backwards fill-mode affects the starting state.
steps.hint: Set animation-delay to a positive value like 2s or 2000ms on the fourth div's rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The fourth div will start with the animation's first keyframe style during the delay period, showing backwards fill-mode behavior.
successCriteria: animation-delay property is added to the fourth div's rule
animation-delay has a positive time value (e.g., 2s)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added animation-delay with a positive time value to the fourth div's rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The animation-delay property is missing or incorrect. Add animation-delay with a positive time value to the fourth div's rule.

steps.title: Create visual labels and final polish
steps.instruction: Add descriptive text labels above each box to show which animation-fill-mode and animation-direction values are applied.
steps.hint: You can add paragraph elements before each div with text describing the animation properties used for that box.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each animated box will have a clear text label above it indicating which animation-fill-mode and animation-direction values are being demonstrated.
successCriteria: Four paragraph elements are added with descriptive text for each animation example, making the demonstration self-explanatory.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some labels, but make sure all four boxes have descriptive text above them.
steps.feedbackWrong: The labels are missing or incomplete. Add paragraph elements with text describing the animation properties for each box.
